The Drums Agreed to Wait

STS-MS7-L4-1400P-MSVPA-PTN-CFI-01 • MS Visual and Performing Arts Music Grade 7 • Revising Music from Criteria and Feedback
Look at the picture. You will answer some questions about it. Press the play button to hear each question. Record your answer for each question. You can listen to your answer and record it again. Click SUBMIT RECORDINGS when you have answered all the questions.
JUST FOR FUN · OPTIONAL
A treaty is what two sides sign when neither one gets everything it wanted. Mika, Esteban, and Camila brought two music traditions into one room: a taiko drum on one side, a trumpet and a guitarron on the other. Every term on their treaty came from something a classmate wrote on the feedback wall after hearing the first draft, and the criteria board is what they agreed to judge the piece by. Nobody changed the music because they were told to. They changed it because they could say why.
If you wrote the next term of the treaty, what would you change about the piece, and which note on the feedback wall would be your reason?
Optional. You do not have to record this one.
1
What is Mika doing?
Look at the picture. Justify what Mika is doing and connect it to the standards the group set for itself.
2
What is Esteban holding?
Look at the picture. Justify what Esteban holds and explain why blending two traditions takes agreement from both sides.
3
What is the teacher doing?
Look at the picture. Justify the teacher's action and explain what the group gave up to reach it.
4
What room is this? How do you know?
Look at the picture. Justify what room this is and explain how the wall displays support the work being done.
5
Tell me about the feedback wall.
Look at the picture. Justify how honest comments become real revisions, using the wall as your evidence.
6
What is Camila wearing?
Look at the picture. Justify Camila's part in the group using every clue you can see about her.
Record an answer for each question, then submit.
Content alignment: MU:Cr3.1.7b — Describe the rationale for making revisions to the music based on evaluation criteria and feedback from teacher and peers. ELD (Speaking — official ELPAC “Talk About a Scene”): PI.A.1, PII.B.3, PII.B.4, PII.B.5.
